target_customer: B2B SaaS product and engineering teams building CRM integrations for their customers
problem: Every customer used a different CRM, so SaaS teams rebuilt the same integrations and authorization flows again and again.
business_model: Developer API subscription; a directory listing shows plans from $29 per month

founders.name: Trey Griffith
previous_startups: Sparkswap (Bitcoin Lightning exchange, raised $3.5M in 2019, ceased operations March 2020 per search results)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is now Head of Engineering at Clipboard Health.

competitors.name: Tray.io
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the summary found

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalizing many CRM APIs, custom objects and OAuth flows is steady integration engineering with ongoing maintenance.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded, integrations are sticky, but unified API products are copyable and larger iPaaS players competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later years saw many universal API vendors such as Merge raise money; Xkit left no public exit.

market_need_then: Not documented by a source dated near 2018. A StackShare listing describes Xkit as handling third-party authorization for 20 plus services but gives no date.

branding.domain_note: Used xkit.co. That domain now redirects to getxkit.com, a page for an unrelated Twitter cleanup tool.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand evidence found, and the name is shared with other Xkit and Kit products such as Shopify's Kit CRM.

branding.community_and_virality: A DEV Community organization profile exists for Xkit.

outcome_analysis: Xkit offered one API for connecting to customers' CRMs and went Inactive per the YC directory, while its founder moved on to Clipboard Health. No shutdown notice, acquisition or funding round was found, so the cause is not public. PitchBook lists a July 2025 secondary transaction and about three employees, so the company may have continued quietly for years before the xkit.co domain changed hands.
notes: Cause of inactivity not public. PitchBook reports $3.62M raised, but this likely duplicates the total of Sparkswap, the founder's earlier company, so it is not recorded as a round. Tray.io is a loose competitor since it is a general automation platform; its date and amount come from a search summary of its June 2018 release. YC page lists one founder. Education not found.
